The working-tree blobs match head tree faa52bb (clean_checkout.py c203574, test file 63dbe3c). I copied the head file to scratch and drove main() with a fake subprocess layer (no Docker) through every path. All OK, no remove: rc 0, last line '25/25 steps ok', 0 rmi. All OK with --remove-images: rc 0, 25/25, 10 rmi, one per built ref. One build fails: rc 1, '23/25 steps ok; FAILED: build safety-service, probe ... (not run: no built image)', 9 rmi. Every build fails: rc 1, 0/25, no rmi, no TypeError. A probe fails: rc 1, 23/25, 10 rmi. A ref re-tagged to another id: 9 rmi, that ref left alone. Inspect rc 1: 0 rmi, which leaks but never deletes. KeyboardInterrupt on the 3rd build: the exception propagates and exactly the 2 built refs are rmi'd. --compose: 26/26. --tests: 26/26. --compose --tests: 27/27. Every path with --remove-images untagged exactly the refs it built, each as `docker rmi <ref>` with no -f and no sha256. The cleanup() change (`run = run or subprocess.run`) leaves production behaviour as it was: main() still calls the real subprocess.run, and an injected callable still wins. It only moves the lookup from import time to call time. Read-only `docker image ls` shows no clean-* images, and the e399b3b export marker holds the full tree id, which matches the implementer's real-Docker claim.

findings.problem: This predates fix3 and is not a regression of this round. export_tree() reuses an earlier export with a plain `shutil.rmtree(out)`. A `--tests` run gives the export a private git context (`git init` plus `git add -A`), and Git for Windows writes the loose objects read-only. Python 3.12's rmtree raises PermissionError on them. It also deletes the alphabetically-first `.clean-checkout-export` marker before it reaches `.git`, so the directory is left half-deleted and without a marker.
findings.failure_scenario: Run `clean_checkout.py --tree X --tests`, then rerun any mode for the same tree with the default out D:\tmp\mvp-exec\clean-checkout\<tree7> or the same --out. The rerun crashes in export_tree with `PermissionError [WinError 5] Access is denied: ...\.git\objects\..`. Every later run then stops with `refusing to reuse <out>: it is not empty and is not an earlier export` until the operator deletes the directory by hand and clears the read-only attributes. Both fail loud with a non-zero rc, and no false pass is produced. Neither the gate test nor the W0 barrier `--compose` run uses --tests.
findings.fix: Clear the read-only bit and retry in rmtree, e.g. `shutil.rmtree(out, onexc=lambda f, p, e: (os.chmod(p, stat.S_IWRITE), f(p)))`. Alternatively, delete everything except the marker first and remove the marker last, so a failed delete stays reusable. Add a unit test: _git_context(out), then export_tree into the same out.
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy of the head file (Python 3.12.3, venv): I wrote the marker and a file, ran clean_checkout._git_context(out) (1 read-only object file appeared), then ran export_tree('HEAD^{tree}', out, repo). Result: `PermissionError [WinError 5] Access is denied: ...rerun-out\.git\objects\58\7be6b4...`. Afterwards the marker was gone and 2 entries were left. A third export_tree raised `SystemExit refusing to reuse ...: it is not empty and is not an earlier export`. The scratch directory is deleted. Prior WS-01.9 reviews never mention rmtree, read-only files or PermissionError.

votes.reason: I reproduced the failure. `export_tree` calls a plain `shutil.rmtree(out)` at line 166, and `--tests` runs `_git_context(out)` at line 254, which creates a `.git` directory inside the export. In a scratch repo (`git init`, then `git add -A`), Python 3.12.3 `shutil.rmtree('.git')` raised `PermissionError [WinError 5]` on a loose object file. Nothing in the code clears the read-only bit. A rerun on the same tree or `--out` would therefore crash, and the half-deleted directory would lose its marker. Both outcomes fail loud with a non-zero rc and produce no false pass, so "minor" is the right severity. The gate test and the `--compose` barrier run don't use `--tests`, so they are unaffected. I did not run `export_tree` itself, and I did not confirm that the marker is deleted first.

prior_findings.note: ok = _run(...) rename is in place. The new offline main() test fails when I revert it to built = _run(...) (3 failures in a scratch copy), so it catches the bool rebinding. Current suite: 54 passed, 1 skipped.

test_mvp_008_main_drives_every_step_offline_and_cleans_up_by_reference drives main() offline. It asserts tree-ish resolution before export, 'N/N steps ok', rmi by ref without -f or sha, and probes run by image id. It fails when I add -f to rmi.
run() prints 'tag: <name>', and the main test asserts 'tag: clean-<7>-' appears in stdout.

findings.problem: C1 (shrunken registry) has no behavioural test. test_mvp_008_c1 only checks that the flag is parsed and that 'require-registry-match' appears in the Makefile and the ps1 script. The main() test passes --require-registry-match, but its fake registry equals IMAGES, so the mismatch branch never runs.
findings.failure_scenario: If the `if require_registry_match:` guard in run() is neutralised (I replaced it with `if False:` in a scratch copy), the mismatch only warns and the proof stays green with a shrunken export registry. All c1 and main tests still passed: the failure set was identical to the baseline, whose 2 failures come from files missing in the scratch copy.
findings.fix: Add an offline test that makes load_registry return IMAGES[:-1] and calls run() or main() with require_registry_match=True. Assert rc == 1, '[FAIL] --require-registry-match' in stdout, and that no docker build was issued.
findings.evidence: The scratch mutation `if False:` left the same two scratch-only failures as the unmodified baseline. No test exercises the registry-mismatch return.

findings.problem: C2 (GIT_* leak) is tested only through _git_context, plus tests_env. The git_env(os.environ) wiring in resolve_tree and export_tree (git archive) is not covered.
findings.failure_scenario: If someone removes env=git_env(os.environ) from resolve_tree, or from the git archive call, an operator's GIT_DIR or GIT_INDEX_FILE would redirect tree resolution or export to a foreign repo. In a scratch copy I dropped env= from resolve_tree's subprocess.run, and the suite result was unchanged from baseline. The main test fakes subprocess.run, so it never checks the env passed to it.
findings.fix: Add a test that sets GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE to a foreign repo and calls resolve_tree(tree, repo) and export_tree(tree, out, repo). Assert they resolve against `repo`. Alternatively, have the fake run in the main test assert that the env kwarg for git calls contains no GIT_* keys.
findings.evidence: Mutating resolve_tree's `env=git_env(os.environ)` away left test results identical to baseline. The test names that exist (c2_git_calls_ignore..., main_drives...) do not reach that call's real env.

votes.reason: run() in scripts/ci/clean_checkout.py returns 1 when --require-registry-match is set and the export's registry differs (lines 223-227). The main() test passes the flag, but its fake load_registry returns list(IMAGES), so the mismatch branch is never taken. test_mvp_008_c1 only checks flag parsing and the presence of the flag text in the Makefile and ps1 script. No test asserts rc==1 or the '[FAIL] --require-registry-match' output for a shrunken registry, so neutralising the guard would leave the tests green. This is a real but minor coverage gap.

votes.reason: The gap is real. resolve_tree (line 66) and the git archive call (line 169) both pass env=git_env(os.environ). Test c2 (lines 320-337) only calls _git_context and tests_env, with GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE set. The N2 test (lines 302-317) calls resolve_tree with no GIT_* variables set. The main test's fake_run takes **_kw and never inspects env, and export_tree is replaced by fake_export. So no test reaches the env= wiring in resolve_tree or in the archive call. A GIT_DIR set in the environment overrides git -C, so dropping env= would let the operator's variable redirect tree resolution or export. Nothing would catch that. I did not run the suite or a mutation here. The claim rests on reading the code, and the mutation result is the finding's own report. Minor severity is right: it is a regression-guard gap, not a live defect.
